fact: The Sfax Court of Appeal sentenced journalist Haythem El Mekki to one year in prison on 15 July 2026, requalifying the case from Decree-Law 54 to Article 86 of the Telecommunications Code, over a social-media post on the situation at a Sfax hospital (complaint by the hospital); a first-instance court had dismissed it.
Lawyer and commentator Sonia Dahmani was arrested in May 2024 and later convicted several times for remarks made on broadcast programmes, per Nawaat.

Journalists Borhen Bsaies and Mourad Zeghidi were sentenced to one year in prison, reduced to eight months, for statements under Decree-Law 54; the document gives no date for the sentence, so the document's publication date 2026-07-16 is used.

The National Union of Tunisian Journalists (SNJT), with Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International and RSF, denounced Decree-Law 2022-54 as a tool of repression, and the SNJT called for the annulment of the El Mekki judgment; the SNJT is inside the country; the criticism is reported in the document dated 2026-07-16.
RSF reports that on 15 July 2026 journalist and columnist Haythem El Mekki was sentenced to one year in prison over a post denouncing conditions in a hospital morgue.
RSF says that in 2024 over ten journalists in Tunisia were targeted by legal proceedings for doing their jobs, among them Mourad Zeghidi, held since 11 May 2024.
RSF says the radio station Diwan FM keeps a balanced, critical approach to the political news cycle; no named policy is given and no date, so the document's publication date 2026-04-30 is used.
